campaign.title: Second Solarist
campaign.hook: Sixty years ago the First Solarist sailed past the edge of every chart and never came home. Captain Aurel Vance is leading a convoy to finish what they started. Since his broadcast, your whole crew has been dreaming of a white shore.

muster.name: Halcyon Relay
muster.desc: A grey moon with a great old relay station on it, strung with flags. The Second Solarist convoy gathers here.

first-claim.name: Tamsel
first-claim.desc: A gentle green world the old charts call Tamsel. It is about to be given a new name.

harrow.name: Harrow
harrow.desc: A cold, bright world of ice fields and blue crevasses, where the convoy stops to make repairs.

shallows.name: The Shallows
shallows.desc: An ocean so shallow you could wade across most of it, warm and green and full of slow light.

cinder.name: Cinder
cinder.desc: A black and burning world at the edge of the charts. The last place anyone has a name for.

white-shore.name: The White Shore
white-shore.desc: A world of white sand under a black, starless sky. Everybody aboard has seen it before, in their sleep.

episodes.title: The broadcast
text: Every ship in the sector hears it at once. A warm, enormous voice, the kind of voice that has given a lot of speeches: "This is Captain Aurel Vance. Sixty years ago the First Solarist sailed past the edge of every chart, and never came home. I am going to finish what they started. I am calling it the Second Solarist. And I want you with me."

In the galley of {ship}, nobody speaks for a moment. Then {Crew} says, very quietly, that {crew.they} had a strange dream last night. A white shore. A black sky. And a voice that said almost exactly the same thing.

episodes.title: Halcyon Relay
text: The convoy gathers at {world}: thirty ships, maybe more, strung with flags, their crews swarming the old relay station like a festival. Everyone is young. Everyone is hopeful. Everyone has a story about the First Solarist they heard as a child.

And there is Vance himself, on a crate in the middle of the crowd: tall, silver-haired, a coat with too many buttons, shaking every hand twice. Behind him stands a tired woman with a clipboard who is clearly doing all the actual work. Her badge says Mira Osei, First Officer.

choice.prompt: Vance wants {ship} to sign up on the spot. Sign now, or talk to Mira Osei first?

options.label: Sign now
options.reply: Vance pumps your hand and calls {ship} "the finest little vessel I have ever seen". He has said this to four ships today. It still feels good.

options.label: Talk to Mira first
options.reply: Mira looks surprised to be asked anything. "Supplies for eight months. Charts for four. He thinks the rest will turn up." She pauses. "Sign anyway. He needs ships that ask questions."

episodes.title: The speech
text: On the last night before departure, Vance gives a speech from the top of the relay tower. It is very long. It mentions the First Solarist eleven times and himself thirty-four times. {Crew} counts.

But some of it is beautiful. He talks about the edge of the charts like a coastline nobody has walked, and about what it would mean to be the people who finally walk it. Half the convoy is crying by the end. A young pilot near {ship} called Tamsin Rook is crying hardest of all.
That night {Crew} dreams of the white shore again. It is closer this time.

episodes.title: The shared dream
text: At breakfast, someone mentions the dream. Then someone else. Then everybody: the whole crew of {ship} has been dreaming the same thing, every night since the broadcast. White sand. Black sky without a single star. Waves that make no sound.
And standing at the edge of the water, always with their back turned, a figure in an old Solarist flight jacket.

choice.prompt: Tell the rest of the convoy about the dream, or keep it to yourselves?

options.label: Tell the convoy
options.reply: You mention it over the radio, half joking. The channel goes silent. Then, one by one, other ships answer. They have been dreaming it too. All of them.

options.label: Keep it to yourselves
options.reply: You keep it. But that night you hear Tamsin Rook on the open channel, talking in her sleep: "white sand," she says, "white sand," and then, clearly, your ship's name.

episodes.title: Departure
text: Thirty-one ships light their engines at once. From the relay it must look like a new constellation, sliding off the edge of the sky.

The first days are glorious. Vance broadcasts music to the whole convoy. Ships race each other through the asteroid belts. Tamsin Rook flies loops around {ship} until Mira tells her, over the open channel, to stop showing off. She stops showing off for about an hour.

episodes.title: Tamsel
text: The first world past the edge of the old charts is soft and green and gentle, with long white beaches. Its old name, from a survey a century ago, is {world}.

Vance lands first, of course. He plants a flag. Then he turns to the cameras and says, "I name this world Vance's Rest." The convoy cheers. {Crew} looks at Mira Osei, who is staring very hard at her clipboard.

choice.prompt: Vance asks the convoy to raise a toast to Vance's Rest. Raise it, or stay quiet?

options.label: Raise the toast
options.reply: You raise a cup. Vance beams across the beach at {ship} and raises his back. Mira writes something down.

options.label: Stay quiet
options.reply: You keep your cup down. Nobody notices, except Vance, who notices everything about himself. Later, Mira passes {ship} on the beach and says, without stopping, "Thank you."

episodes.title: Rook
text: Tamsin Rook turns up at {ship}'s hatch in the middle of the night with a broken fuel line in her hands and a look on her face like she is about to be in very serious trouble.
"I pushed the engines too hard," she says. "Racing. If Vance finds out, he'll leave me behind. He leaves people behind. He says the Second Solarist can't carry passengers."

choice.prompt: Help Rook fix it quietly, or tell her to report it to Mira?

options.label: Fix it quietly
options.reply: You fix it together in the dark with the ship's spare parts. By dawn the line is good as new and Rook has eaten half the galley's biscuits. She calls {ship} "home base" after that.

options.label: Tell her to report it
options.reply: Rook goes pale, but she goes. Mira fixes the line herself, says nothing to Vance, and docks Rook's racing privileges for a week. Rook is furious, then grateful, in that order.

episodes.title: Logs
text: Every evening Vance broadcasts the day's log to the whole convoy, and from there back to the relay, and from there to the whole sector. Everyone back home is listening.
Tonight's log describes the landing on Vance's Rest. In it, there was a storm. There was a moment of great danger. Vance made a daring choice and saved the landing party.
There was no storm. {Crew} was there. It was a lovely, calm afternoon.

episodes.title: The dream, closer
text: The dream is different tonight. The figure in the flight jacket is closer to the shore, and when {Crew} tries to walk towards them, the white sand pulls at {crew.their} feet like deep snow.

In the morning, the whole convoy's course has shifted by a few degrees. Nobody ordered it. Every navigator on every ship checks their instruments. Every instrument says they are flying straight. Vance says it is destiny. Mira says it is a fault in the charts, and stays up all night trying to find it.

episodes.title: Past the last chart
text: Tonight the convoy crosses the last line on any chart that anybody has. Vance makes it a ceremony: every ship flashes its lights at once, and he reads the names of the First Solarist's crew, one by one, into the dark.

text.text: He reads them beautifully. When he finishes, he adds a thirteenth name, his own. Nobody knows what to say. You find you raised your cup again without meaning to.
He reads them beautifully. When he finishes, he adds a thirteenth name, his own. Nobody knows what to say. Across the dark, Mira's ship blinks its lights at {ship}, once, like a small private signal.

text: That night everybody in the convoy has the same dream, and for the first time the figure on the shore turns around. Nobody can remember their face in the morning. Only that they were smiling, and that they looked very, very tired.

episodes.title: Harrow
text: Two months past the edge. The convoy stops at a cold bright world of blue ice to mend its engines. Vance names it after himself, again: Vance's Glory. Then, a week later, Vance's Patience. He seems to have forgotten he already named it.
The crews are tired now. The music broadcasts have stopped. Rations were cut last week, quietly, by Mira. {Crew} has started keeping a private log, in pencil, of what actually happens each day.

episodes.title: The rewritten log
text: Vance's broadcast tonight describes a disaster on Harrow: an ice-quake, a crevasse, a ship in peril, and Vance himself, roped to the edge, pulling the crew to safety one by one.
It was {ship}. It was {ship}'s crew who did the roping and the pulling, last Tuesday, while Vance was asleep. In the log he has made it his story, every word.

choice.prompt: Send the true account back to the relay yourselves, or let his version stand?

options.label: Send the truth
options.reply: You send the true account to the relay, plainly, without any adjectives. Vance doesn't mention it. But the next morning, {ship}'s place in the convoy has moved to the very back.

options.label: Let it stand
options.reply: You let it stand. It is only a story, you tell yourselves. Back home, children are already playing at being Aurel Vance on the ice.

episodes.title: The Shallows
text: The next world is all water, warm and shallow and green, with slow lights moving under the surface. It is so peaceful that the whole convoy stops for three days and just floats.
The crews swim. Rook teaches {Crew} to dive for the glowing shells. For three days, nobody talks about the First Solarist at all, and everybody is happier than they have been in months.
Vance hates it. On the fourth morning he orders the convoy on, an hour before dawn, without warning.

episodes.title: The ship that fell behind
text: One ship doesn't answer the dawn call: a little cargo hauler, the Persimmon, with a crew of three and a cracked engine. They are still floating in the Shallows, calling for help.
Vance won't turn back. "The Second Solarist does not slow down for anybody," he broadcasts. "The First Solarist never did." Mira argues with him on the open channel until he cuts her off.

choice.prompt: Go back for the Persimmon alone, or stay with the convoy?

options.label: Go back for them
options.reply: {Ship} breaks formation and goes back. It takes two days to fix the Persimmon's engine and two more to catch up. When you rejoin the convoy, three other ships have quietly moved to fly beside {ship}.

options.label: Stay with the convoy
options.reply: You stay. Mira takes her own ship back for them instead, against orders. She comes back four days later, towing the Persimmon, and doesn't speak to anybody for a while.

episodes.title: Mira
text: Mira Osei comes aboard {ship} late one night, for the first time, and sits in the galley with a cup of tea she doesn't drink.

"I've known him twenty years," she says. "He was the bravest pilot I ever saw. He just wanted to be remembered. Everybody wants that a bit. He wants it so much it's eating him." She turns the cup round and round. "The supplies won't last. If we don't turn back soon, we can't."

choice.prompt: Mira is asking, without quite asking, whose side {ship} is on. Hers, or Vance's?

options.label: Mira's
options.reply: You tell her. She nods slowly, like someone putting down something heavy. "Then we're going to need more ships," she says. "Quietly."

options.label: Vance's
options.reply: You tell her the captain should have his chance. Mira smiles, very tiredly. "So did I, once. Twenty years ago." She leaves her tea behind, still full.

episodes.title: The figure on the shore
text: The dream has changed again. Now everyone in the convoy is on the white shore together, thousands of them, standing in the silent waves. And the figure in the flight jacket is walking down the beach towards {Crew}.

It is the First Solarist's captain. {Crew} knows it the way you know things in dreams. She stops a few steps away, and she says, very kindly: "You can stay, you know. It's what you want. It's what everyone wants, in the end."
{Crew} wakes up shouting. So do half the crews in the convoy.

episodes.title: Hunger
text: The rations are half what they were. The convoy is flying on fumes and stubbornness. Two ships have turned back in the night without telling anyone.

Vance broadcasts every evening now, longer and longer, about the glory waiting at the end of the journey. He looks thin. He has started wearing a First Solarist flight jacket he had made, with his own name stitched on it.

choice.prompt: {Ship} has more food left than most. Share it with the convoy, or keep it for your own crew?

options.label: Share it
options.reply: You share it out ship by ship. It doesn't go far. But Rook flies a loop around {ship} for the first time in weeks, and on the open channel, somebody starts singing.

options.label: Keep it
options.reply: You keep it. Your crew eats well and feels terrible. That night {Crew} takes half {crew.their} dinner across to Rook's ship anyway, without telling anyone.

episodes.title: Rook's dream
text: Tamsin Rook doesn't wake up.

Her crew finds her in her bunk, smiling, breathing slowly, deep in the dream. Nothing wakes her: not noise, not cold water, not Mira shouting her name. On the third day, two more pilots don't wake up either.

text.text: {Crew} sits by Rook's bunk for a whole session, holding her hand, telling her about the biscuits she ate on {ship} the night you fixed her fuel line. Once, very faintly, she smiles at the right moment.
{Crew} sits by Rook's bunk for a whole session. Once, very faintly, she says "Mira," in her sleep, and frowns, the way she did when she was told to report her broken fuel line.

episodes.title: Cinder
text: The last world anyone has a name for is black and burning: rivers of fire under a dim red sun. The convoy stops at its edge because there is nowhere else to stop.

Vance stands on a ridge above the lava and makes his longest speech yet. Beyond Cinder, he says, the white shore is waiting. He has seen it in his dreams. The First Solarist found it, and now he will. He doesn't mention Rook. He doesn't mention the ships that turned back. He doesn't mention food.

episodes.title: The vote
text: Mira calls a meeting, for the first time ever, of every captain in the convoy. Vance is not invited.

text.text: {Ship} is there, and most of the captains turn to look at you when they arrive. The Persimmon's captain says, simply: "{Ship} came back for us." It is the first thing anybody says.
{Ship} is there. The captains look at Mira, mostly. She has been carrying this convoy for months. Everyone knows it but Vance.

text: The question is simple. Turn back now, while there is still food enough to make it home. Or go on, past Cinder, to the white shore, and find out what the First Solarist found, and wake Rook and the others, if they can be woken.
The vote is a tie. Every face in the room turns to {ship}.

episodes.title: Beyond Cinder
text: The convoy goes on. Not because Vance said so, but because of Rook and the others, asleep in their bunks, and because there is no other way to wake them.
Past Cinder there are no stars. Not few: none. The dark outside is absolute, and the instruments read nothing at all, and every night now the whole convoy sleeps on the same white beach.

episodes.title: The mutiny that wasn't

text.text: The captains who voted with Mira want to take the convoy from Vance. They ask {ship} to lead it.
Some of the captains want to take the convoy from Vance. They don't trust {ship} to help: you stood by him. But they ask you to stay out of their way.

text: Vance finds out, of course. He always finds out things about himself. He doesn't rage. He goes very quiet and very small, and broadcasts, to the whole convoy: "I only wanted it to mean something. I only wanted us to matter." Then he goes off the air.
Nobody takes the convoy. Nobody has the heart.

episodes.title: The shore
text: And then, one morning, it is there: a world with no sun, glowing faintly by itself, white from pole to pole. Under the black sky, a white shore. Exactly as everyone has dreamed it.

The whole convoy lands on the beach together. The waves make no sound. The sand is warm. Standing in the shallows, in rows, motionless, facing the sea, are people. Dozens of them, in old Solarist flight jackets. The First Solarist's crew.

episodes.title: The sleepers
text: They are alive. Asleep on their feet, breathing slowly, sixty years older than in any photograph, and smiling. Every one of them is smiling.
Mira walks down the line, reading the names off their jackets in a whisper. They are all here. All twelve.

The shore is dreaming, {Crew} realises. The whole world is one long slow dream, and it has been reaching out across the dark for sixty years, offering every sleeper the one thing they want most. The First Solarist came, and it gave them what they wanted, and they stayed.

episodes.title: What Vance wants
text: Vance walks into the shallows as if somebody has called his name. He stops beside the First Solarist's captain, and his face goes soft, and his eyes close.

In the dream, everybody sees it at once: Vance on a stage under a sky full of lights, with the whole sector applauding, forever. Statues. Songs. Every chart with his name on every world. It is the saddest thing {Crew} has ever seen.

choice.prompt: Wade in after Vance now, or first try to wake the First Solarist's captain?

options.label: Go after Vance
options.reply: You go in up to your knees. The water is warm and makes no sound, and it pulls at your thoughts like sleep. You reach Vance and take his arm. He doesn't notice. Not yet.

options.label: Wake the captain first
options.reply: You shake the First Solarist's captain gently by the shoulders. Her eyes open, very slowly. "Oh," she says, sixty years late. "You came. I hoped somebody would." She looks at Vance and sighs. "Him too? Poor man."

episodes.title: The captain's story

text.text: The First Solarist's captain sits on the warm sand, wrapped in a blanket from {ship}, and tells it simply. "We were desperate to matter. To be the ones who went furthest. The shore saw that, and it gave us what we wanted, and it was so lovely we never woke up. It isn't cruel. It's kind. It's just kind in the wrong way."

Holding Vance's arm in the shallows, {Crew} hears a voice in the dream: the First Solarist's captain, speaking from somewhere behind {crew.their} eyes. "We were desperate to matter. The shore saw that, and gave us what we wanted, and we never woke up. It isn't cruel. It's just kind in the wrong way."

text: "Rook and the others are already here," she says. "In the dream. They wanted to be heroes. The shore made them heroes." She looks at the convoy ships on the beach. "And it will take the rest of you, one by one, if you stay long enough."

episodes.title: Desperation
text: Half the convoy is asleep now. They stand in the shallows in long rows, smiling, beside the First Solarist. The ones still awake have to hold each other's hands to stay that way. Mira hasn't slept in two days.
The shore is gentle and patient and everywhere. When {Crew} closes {crew.their} eyes, even for a second, there it is: whatever {crew.they} {crew:wants|want} most in the world, waiting, warm, so easy.

text.text: What keeps {ship}'s crew awake, in the end, is small: the memory of sharing out the last food, and somebody singing on the open channel. Things that mattered without anybody watching.
What keeps {ship}'s crew awake, in the end, is each other. Somebody talks. Somebody makes tea. Somebody keeps their hand on the next person's shoulder all night.

episodes.title: The way out
text: The First Solarist's captain knows how to leave. You can't be dragged out of the dream, she says. You have to be given a reason to want something else more.
For Rook, it is easy: {Crew} tells her about the biscuits, and the loops she flew, and the people waiting for her back on the Persimmon. She wakes up crying and laughing and asking what she missed.
One by one, the crews are woken, each with a reason. It takes all night. And then there is only Vance, standing in the shallows, smiling at applause that will never stop.

episodes.title: The last choice
text: There isn't enough time to do everything. The shore is pulling harder now, as if it knows. The ships need to lift before the tide of sleep takes the crews again.

Mira is standing beside {ship}'s hatch with her clipboard, and for the first time in the whole journey she doesn't know what to write. "Twenty years," she says. "I can't leave him. I can't let him keep the convoy here either."

choice.prompt: What do you do about Aurel Vance?

options.label: Wake him, whatever it takes
options.reply: You wade back into the shallows, all of you, and stand around him, and start to talk. Not about glory. About small things: Mira's tea, Rook's loops, the calm afternoon on Tamsel. You keep talking until the sky starts to grey.

options.label: Get the crews home
options.reply: You turn your back on the shore and start the engines. Mira looks at the shallows for a long time. Then she climbs aboard her ship, and doesn't look back.

options.label: Let him have his dream
options.reply: You leave him where he stands, smiling. Mira takes off her First Officer's badge and pins it on his jacket, very gently. "There," she says. "Now you're in charge forever."

episodes.title: Home

text.text: It takes until dawn, if dawn is what you call it here. Then Aurel Vance opens his eyes, and looks around at all of you standing in the water, and says, in a very small voice: "I'm sorry." The convoy flies home together, all thirty-one ships and the First Solarist's twelve. Vance doesn't make a single speech the whole way. When they reach the relay, he lets Mira do the talking. He stands at the back, just one more tired person, and seems, for the first time, perfectly content.

The convoy flies home without him: thirty ships and the First Solarist's twelve, all awake, all alive. Mira is captain now. She keeps the logs plainly, with no adjectives. At the relay, the sector greets the convoy as heroes. Mira tells them the truth: there were no heroes, only people who woke each other up. Nobody puts that on a statue. Everybody remembers it anyway.

The convoy flies home with the First Solarist's twelve, and leaves the Second Solarist's captain on the shore, smiling, forever applauded. The sector tells his story for a hundred years: the captain who went further than anyone and never came back. It is exactly the legend he wanted. Mira never tells anyone that he got it by dreaming.

text: Weeks later, in the galley of {ship}, the dream comes back once, faintly: a white shore, a black sky. But it is empty now. No figures in the shallows. Just quiet water. {Crew} wakes up, makes a cup of tea, and finds {crew.they} {crew:doesn't|don't} want to be anywhere else at all.
